<details>
<summary><strong>Prologue: The Gate</strong> (picks up mid-scene from Session 2)</summary>

::: {.dm-note}
**What this scene actually is.** Varro is not a villain who turned on the party. His
family has carried the shame of Varus's three lost legions in this exact forest for six
generations -- he was already primed to see a second Teutoburg coming before the spear
ever touched him. Its corruption didn't invent his fear, it just agreed with the one he
already carried, until it justified opening a gate and killing a scout. He believes,
right now, that he is saving Rome. Play him as a good man losing a fight he never told
anyone he was having, not as an enemy. Full detail in `CAMPAIGN_LOG.md`.

This scene resumes an in-progress fight -- Ursula engaged Varro at the gate he opened.
Pick it up from there; don't re-stage the whole raid.
:::

**Recap, read or paraphrase:** *"The gate stands open. Varro stands in it, gladius drawn,
blood on his hands that isn't his own -- the scout he killed lies past him, half in the
mud. Ursula is already on him. Whatever the rest of the party was doing when the raid
began, this is what's in front of them now."*

**Varro, corrupted (use his existing stats: AC 17, HP 58):**
- **Gladius** +5 to hit, 1d8+3 slashing
- **Pilum (thrown)**, as per his standard stat block
- **The god's hand steadies him:** once per round, Varro may reroll one failed attack
  roll or saving throw. This is Mars's influence lending him just enough to keep fighting
  -- not a fair fight, but not an unbeatable one either.
- He is not trying to escape or to win a war. He is trying to hold the gate shut against
  Rome's own future mistake. He will not flee. He will not surrender to a threat of
  force. He will only stop for the third option below.

**Three ways this ends (any one of them):**

1. **He is killed or dropped to 0 HP.** He does not beg. His last words, quiet, almost
   relieved: *"Tell them I did this for Rome."* He believes it to the end.
2. **He is captured -- subdued, restrained, or surrenders after being clearly beaten.**
   He goes without further violence once it's clear the fight is lost, but says nothing
   useful under guard. He is not lying when he refuses to explain himself. He does not
   have the words for what happened to him.
3. **Someone breaks through to him.** DC 16 Wisdom (Insight) or Charisma (Persuasion)
   (active: naming what he actually is afraid of -- Varus, the lost legions, this exact
   forest -- rather than accusing him of treason), as a group action any character can
   contribute to once per round. On success, Varro staggers, drops the gladius, and says,
   *"I can still hear it. Get it away from me. Get it away from all of us."* He survives,
   devastated by what he nearly did, and is in no state to travel with the party into the
   forest -- he stays behind, relieved of duty, watched. This is the option that costs the
   party nothing but gives them no clean resolution either: Varro lives, but he is not
   coming with them, and the fort has lost its most trusted officer regardless.

**Whichever ending occurs: Varro does not travel with the party into the forest.** Any
later reference to him in this chapter or its GM tools assumes his absence -- update
those on sight if you find one that still assumes he's present.

**Lucius is already in command.** This is not a new development -- it happened in
Session 2, already played, and needs no scene to re-establish it here. As Session 3
opens, Tribune Lucius has been the fort's commanding officer for some time, Varro's
authority already suspended, Corvinus's standing already under review. He appears at
the gate in the aftermath of the fight below simply because he commands the fort now
and this is fort business, not because he is arriving to seize anything.

If it's useful to ground the table in where things stand, a single line covers it: *"Get
this cleaned up. I want the garrison steady before nightfall."* -- said the way a man
gives an order he has given a hundred times already, not the way a man announces new
authority. He carries a small locked box he does not set down and does not explain. If
anyone asks about it directly: *"That is not fort business."*

::: {.dm-note}
Play Lucius arrogant and controlled here, not cruel. He is performing certainty he does
not fully have -- his real orders say bring it back, his real conviction (formed
somewhere his father never knew about) says it must never leave. The lockbox is
personal, not political; do not pre-decide its contents. This is the same suspicious,
observing Lucius from Session 1, now with real authority and something to lose, and that
authority is old news to him by now, not a fresh performance.
:::

**Lucius comes with them.** He does not trust "Imperial property" of this significance to
anyone else's hands after what just happened, and delegates the fort's day-to-day
command to a subordinate for the duration. This is not generosity -- it's the same
control instinct that got him into command in the first place, and it's the only way
his own real orders from Rome ("recover the weapon") get satisfied in person rather than
by report. Every existing reference to Lucius traveling with the party through the rest
of this chapter (the river crossing, the grove, the citizenship co-sponsor mechanic)
still holds -- this is the reason why.

**Transition:** the party is given leave to depart for the forest -- whether Lucius
frames this as a mission he's ordering them on, or something he's letting them do
because stopping them would cost him more than he can currently afford, is a live
choice for the table. Either way, they leave with a fresh, unresolved wound instead of a
clean goodbye. Proceed to Scene 0 below; the two-day travel montage picks up from here.

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 0: Cold Open</strong> (5 minutes)</summary>

**Start in media res — the camp is wrong.**

They've been traveling for two days. They're camped in a clearing that should feel safe. It doesn't.

**Read aloud:**

> *You wake before dawn. The forest is completely silent.*
>
> *Not quiet — silent. No birds. No insects. No wind in the branches. The kind of silence that has weight.*
>
> *The spear is glowing.*
>
> *A faint red light pulses from its wrappings like a heartbeat. Around the cart carrying it — the dead zone. Everything within five feet of it is still. A leaf is frozen mid-fall between the spear and the ground.*
>
> *One of your companions is standing beside it. They've been there for some time. They aren't moving.*
>
> *On a nearby tree, carved deep into the bark, words in Latin:*
>
> **MARS VIDET OMNIA**

**DM Direction:** The companion standing by the spear is the NPC the party trusts most — or whichever party member drew the short straw privately (see DM Notes). They don't remember getting up. When questioned, they're genuinely confused and frightened. They didn't do it consciously. Not yet.

Don't resolve this. Just put it in the air. Cut to Scene 1 immediately.

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 1: Something is Wrong</strong></summary>

Three dead birds lie near the camp perimeter. Then the party finds the handout — Handout 7, carved into a tree. One of their NPCs made it. They don't know they did.

<details>
<summary><strong>Identifying the Influenced Character</strong></summary>

The spear's influence is gradual. One NPC in the party is being slowly possessed — not controlled, but *pulled*. The DM should pass a folded note to that player at session start (see DM Notes for the note's contents). The player knows; the other characters don't.

**Three ways to identify the influenced NPC before they act:**

**Clue 1: The Physical Signs**
Perception DC 13 (passive, during travel) or Medicine DC 13 (active: a deliberate physical examination):
- Their eyes have a faint red tinge in direct light
- They've been rubbing the same spot on their arm repeatedly (where they touched the spear in Session 1)
- They're sleeping with their face turned toward where the spear is stored, even if the spear moved
- Medicine specifically: a character who asks to check their pulse or temperature finds a slight fever and dilated pupils that do not match the light level. These are not illness signs. They are arousal signs, the same physiological state as pre-combat readiness -- but the person is calm.

**Clue 2: Their Behaviour**
Insight DC 14 (active: watching them during a specific conversation about the spear or the journey):
- They advocate for keeping the spear more strongly than before, but can't articulate why
- They become visibly agitated when someone else touches or moves the spear
- When asked directly *"Are you alright?"*, there's a micro-pause before they answer

**Clue 2, alternate path:** Hilde, Thusnelda's apprentice (see Scene 2), names the influenced NPC's condition out loud to Thusnelda in Germanic -- quietly, not meant for the party. A character with Germanic language proficiency overhears this exchange and gets the same information Insight DC 14 would have given, no roll required.

**Clue 3: The Spear Reacts**
If the party examines the spear's wrappings or attempts to read its aura: Arcana DC 13 (passive) or Religion DC 14 (passive):
- The spear "leans" -- physically tilts -- in the influenced NPC's direction
- Anyone sensitive to divine energy (Clerics, Paladins) can feel the connection
- Cassia, if present, sees the influence immediately: *"There's a thread between that person and the spear. I missed it. I'm sorry, I missed it."*

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What the Influenced NPC Does if Undetected</strong></summary>

At Scene 4 (the grove), the influenced NPC attempts to stop the ritual — not violently at first, but with increasingly urgent arguments. If not caught, they attempt to take the spear and run at the ritual's climax. They can be brought back with a successful DC 15 Wisdom saving throw from the party (as a group action — holding them, calling to them, breaking the connection through sheer human contact). If the party succeeds, the NPC is devastated by what they nearly did.

</details>

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 2: Thusnelda's Scouts</strong></summary>

Germanic scouts find the party. What happens next depends on Session 2.

**If allied with Vercingetorix:**

> *Four figures appear in the trees. Forest-dark clothes, no armor. One raises a hand — not a weapon.*
>
> *Vercingetorix says, quietly: "My people. We are safe here."*

The scouts offer to take the party to **Thusnelda**, a druid who tends the sacred grove. They know what the party is carrying. They've been expecting them.

*Toll: Information about Roman troop movements along the southern Limes. Moral weight: Sharing this is technically treason. It's also practically necessary.*

**If not allied:**

Perception DC 12 (active: scanning the treeline before the scouts reveal themselves): The undergrowth has been disturbed in a semi-circle to both sides of the trail, with none disturbed directly ahead. The approach pattern is a pincer closing from the flanks, not a block. A soldier who reads this before initiative tells the party their flanks are the threat, not the front -- any character who covers a flank when initiative is called has advantage on the first initiative check.

Ambush — 12 **Tribal Warriors**, 2 **Scouts** (CR 1/2 each) in the tree line. The forest negates Roman tactics: no formations, difficult terrain, low visibility.

Can be ended diplomatically — drop weapons, use Persuasion DC 14 with any Germanic phrase from the player guide, or demonstrate they're trying to destroy the spear (the scouts recognize it and stop). Vercingetorix appears if combat goes 3+ rounds regardless — he's been following.

**Thusnelda** — arriving with the scouts or separately, with two people from the village in tow:

A small, ancient-looking Germanic woman. She carries an oak staff carved with spiraling runes. She smells of pine smoke and something metallic. She looks at the spear and then at the party with the calm gaze of someone who has spent decades looking at hard things.

**Hilde**, her apprentice, a young Cherusci woman, hangs back and watches everything -- this is her first encounter with the spear's corruption and she is not hiding her fascination. She will shadow the party for the rest of Scene 2, asking quiet questions in Germanic to Thusnelda about the influenced NPC by name, not by type. A character with Germanic language proficiency who is paying attention gets Clue 2 for free this way (see Identifying the Influenced Character, above) -- Hilde notices before anyone else does.

**Aldric**, a Germanic man introduced as "one of the village," lingers at the edge of the group and watches too carefully. He is reporting to Senator Brutus, not to Corvinus, and has no idea what the spear actually does -- he was told it is a Roman military asset. Investigation DC 14 (active: noticing how he positions himself to see without being seen) identifies him as something other than a curious local. He leaves before the party departs for the grove -- his information stops here, which is exactly why Brutus's intelligence on this session "ends at the treeline."

> *"God-Killer. Still breathing. I had hoped you would destroy it by now. I see you have not."*

She knows:
- Where the grove is (one full day's travel, through the river, past her teacher's abandoned village)
- That the grove demands a willing sacrifice — not a death, but a loss of something real
- That the ritual will alert Mars. He will come. That cannot be avoided.
- That her teacher attempted this same rite two generations ago, and failed. She has always believed the sacrifice was wrong. She has never had reason to doubt that — until now, standing this close to the spear herself.

She will guide them. She asks nothing in return — this is her purpose.

**Thusnelda speaks like a woman with no time for anything except the truth -- or what she has always believed was the truth:**

> *"The spear belongs to no one. Not the god who made it, not the tribe that used it, not the empire that found it. It belongs to the wound it keeps open. You must close the wound."*

> *"Your friend there" -- she looks at the influenced NPC -- "has a thread in them. Cut it soon. The forest is not kind to loose threads."*

> *"Fear the grove's demand. Most people who come here for the ritual choose something that hurts a little. That is not enough. The grove will know."*

**Additional sample dialogue for Thusnelda across the journey:**

When a character asks her how she knows about the spear: *"My teacher's teacher sealed it. I have been waiting for it to surface since I was eleven years old. I am seventy-three. You are late."*

When someone suggests there might be another way to destroy it: *"There is not, so far as I have ever been taught. The grove is where what was made in divine anger is unmade. I have believed this for sixty years." A pause, small enough most won't catch it. "I have also never actually seen it finished. Only started. And failed."*

When asked what happens to her after the ritual: *"I go back to the grove. I tend it. I wait to see what god pays attention next." A beat. "That has always been the plan. I do not know anymore if it was ever a good one."*

When pressed on whether the ritual always works: *"No. My teacher tried. I watched her fail. I have spent sixty years certain the fault was the sacrifice -- that whoever stood at that altar gave something too small. I was eleven years old. I did not question her explanation, because she was the only explanation I had."*

When someone tries to thank her: *"Do not thank me yet. We have not finished anything."*

**What Thusnelda will and will not say:**

| She will say | She will not say |
|---|---|
| Exactly what the ritual requires | What the "right" sacrifice is for any specific character |
| That the grove rejects insufficient sacrifices | Whether a sacrifice is "good enough" before it is offered |
| That someone in the party is influenced | Who it is -- she knows, but sees this as the party's work to discover |
| What the stakes of failure are | Whether she believes the party will succeed |
| That she has never seen the ritual completed | That she has started to doubt it can be, here -- she hasn't fully admitted this to herself yet |

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 3: The Bridge Crossing</strong></summary>

::: {.dm-note}
**Who is actually driving this scene, and why it should not be a big fight.** Corvinus is not trying to stop the party. Per his secret (see chapter03_npcs.html): he wants the spear destroyed and cannot say so. He also cannot be seen letting armed deserters walk off with contraband -- Brutus has eyes in the fort, and a Legate who visibly lets this go is a Legate who has handed Brutus leverage. So he sends a pursuit that *has* to exist, and quietly makes sure it does not have to succeed: a small escort, vague orders ("prevent the crossing," not "kill them"), and no personal presence. He is not the antagonist of this scene. He is a man threading a needle, and the party's job is to notice that, not to win a battle.

Play this as a small, tense reading of the situation, not a set-piece battle. The "combat," if it happens at all, should resolve in one or two rounds against a handful of unmotivated men -- not a war.
:::

The abandoned village and its ritual site are on the far side of the Vitulans river — currently swollen with spring melt. An old timber bridge spans it at the narrowest point, built by whoever lived in this stretch of forest before Thusnelda's people did and maintained, badly, ever since. The crossing is hard under normal circumstances. It's harder with someone behind you, even if that someone doesn't want to catch you.

**Before the pursuers arrive, this is a good place to let the table breathe.** The bridge is narrow enough that the party crosses in a loose line, not a clump -- good ground for the kind of conversation that doesn't happen when everyone's shoulder to shoulder. Thusnelda, if asked here rather than at camp, answers more personal questions than she has all journey; the influenced NPC's player has room for a quiet, unwatched moment; Hilde asks someone directly what Rome is actually like, since she's never left the forest. Let this run a few unhurried minutes before the escort catches up.

**The bridge:** roughly 90 feet across, planks worn smooth and missing in two places (DC 11 Dexterity (Acrobatics), active: crossing the gaps without falling). The river beneath is fast-moving (DC 13 Strength (Athletics), active: swimming, if someone goes in). Rope can be strung along the rail for anyone struggling (DC 10 Strength (Athletics), active: group action).

**The pursuers arrive:**

If the Legate is pursuing, a small escort catches up exactly when the party is mid-crossing -- not the full weight of the cohort:
- 3 **Legionaries** (use Guard stat blocks)
- 1 **Centurion** (use Knight stat block, CR 3)
- Corvinus himself is never here. He is "one day behind" for the entire session, and stays that way.

**Three tells, for a party paying attention (no roll required to notice all three; DC 11 Wisdom (Insight), passive, to understand what they add up to):**
- The escort is small for a Legate's "advance force" -- four men, not a column.
- They made no effort to approach quietly. The party heard them coming from well up the trail.
- The Centurion's shouted order is "Halt and surrender the item," not "Kill them if they resist" -- a demand for compliance, not a kill order.

**The scene:**
- Half the party is on the far bank, half still crossing or on the near bank when the escort arrives
- If it comes to blows: ranged exchange across the water (half cover for anyone behind the rail), melee on the bridge itself (anyone knocked off: DC 13 Strength (Athletics) to avoid being swept 20 feet downstream). This should be short -- four unmotivated men break off fast once the Centurion is given a reason to.
- The river is impassable to heavy armor (DC 14 Strength save for anyone in metal armor who falls in)

**Ways this resolves without a fight (any one of these ends it):**
- DC 14 Charisma (Intimidation) (active: a centurion-rank character ordering the legionaries to stand down across the water before combat begins): the centurion opposite hesitates -- long enough for the party to cross and hold the bridge. He will not cross without new orders. He does not want this fight either.
- DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion) (active: appealing directly to what the escort's orders actually are, not what they imply): pointing out that "prevent the crossing" was never "kill you for it" gives the Centurion the out he's quietly hoping for. He calls it a "tactical withdrawal" to save face.
- If a character with real Roman political standing is present (the Aasimar Cleric's family name, or any character who has built visible standing with Corvinus) and states it plainly: the Centurion recognizes the name or the authority behind it and treats this as a matter above his pay grade -- he reports the crossing as "unavoidable" rather than a failure, and lets them go.
- Deception DC 15 (active: claiming the mission is sanctioned and the pursuit is unauthorized): requires something tangible -- a document, a seal, or a name the centurion would recognize. Without it, DC 18.

**If the party fights anyway:** it's over in a round or two -- these four men are here to be seen trying, not to die for it. After the first legionary drops or the Centurion takes a solid hit, he calls it: *"Enough. Let them go. I did not sign on to die for a Senator's argument with the gods."* This is not a retreat under pressure so much as a man who was looking for permission to stop.

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 3b: The Farbog</strong></summary>

*(Army of the Damned Part 4 — Into the Farbog, adapted)*

The sacred grove sits on a rise of dry land half a mile past the river. The only path leads through a bog. There is no other route. Thusnelda has been quiet since the crossing.

**Map:** Load `Swamp2` or `SwampPath` the moment the ground turns soft. Switch to `SwampBridges` when the party reaches the plank crossing near the sacrifice site. Switch to `SacredGrove` when the standing stones come into view at the bog's far edge.

**Read aloud:**

> *The ground changes under your feet before you see it. The grass shortens, then disappears. Water appears between the roots. The trees grow thin and angular, their trunks bone-pale, dead branches reaching sideways rather than up.*
>
> *The smell is iron and rot and something sweet underneath. Not pleasant-sweet. The smell of things left here a long time.*
>
> *Thusnelda stops walking. She raises one hand. Silence.*
>
> *"There are old ones here," she says, barely above a whisper. "Do not touch the water. Do not take anything. Do not run. If something approaches — stop and let me speak first."*
>
> *Far ahead, deeper in, a light pulses once. Blue-white. Then dark.*

<details>
<summary><strong>Running the Farbog</strong></summary>

Run one, two, or all three of the encounters below, depending on pacing. Each takes 10-15 minutes. The Myling is the emotional anchor. The Sacrifice Site is the investigation hook. The Hostile Vættir only triggers if the party earns it.

**The trigger tracker:** Keep a mental count of disrespectful acts in the bog (disturbing offerings, attacking the Myling, taking items from the sacrifice site without acknowledgment, ignoring the boundary stone). One: absorbed. Two or more: run the Hostile Vættir encounter.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Encounter A: The Myling</strong></summary>

::: {.dm-note}
The Myling is the spirit of an unbaptized or abandoned child, from Germanic/Norse tradition -- doomed to wander until someone carries its remains to consecrated ground. It is not evil. It is unfinished.

**If combat is forced:** Use the Specter stat block (CR 1), but it does not attack until the second round and only if the party moves away from it. It deals psychic damage. It wails.
:::

A small figure -- child-shaped, translucent, wrong -- stands on a hummock 30 feet off the path. It holds its hands out. It does not approach.

**The party's options:**

- **Ignore it:** It follows, always 20 feet back, never closer. After 10 minutes it begins to weep. DC 13 Wisdom save for anyone who can hear it or gain the Frightened condition (source: the bog itself, not the spirit) for 1 hour. This counts as one disrespect.
- **Acknowledge it (Religion DC 12, active):** Speak the rite of recognition: *"Unnamed one, we see you"* and drop any item of value into the water beside the hummock. The spirit brightens, nods, and stills. It does not follow. Thusnelda exhales quietly.
- **Ask Thusnelda:** She knows the rite. She will recite it if no one else does, but it depletes her: one of her ritual preparation actions in Scene 4 takes an additional round.
- **Attack it:** The spirit dissipates. Two more appear at the next hummock.

**If the party performs the rite correctly and Cassia is present:**

> *Cassia watches the spirit brighten and still. Then quietly: "The Romans burn our dead. The Germans bury theirs with grave goods. We both know the same thing, don't we? That the dead need witness." She does not say this to anyone in particular.*

Let it breathe. This is a character moment, not a mechanics moment.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Encounter B: The Bog Sacrifice Site</strong></summary>

Twenty meters off the path: an offering pole, three meters tall, carved with running knotwork. At its base, offerings wrapped in birch bark. Suspended from the top, partially submerged in the dark water: a preserved human figure, visible only as a shape beneath the surface.

**Investigation DC 13 (active: examining the pole and offerings closely):** This site has been maintained recently. New bark wrappings are visible. The offerings include grain from this season's harvest, bronze pins, and a military sandal buckle -- Roman-made.

::: {.dm-note}
The military sandal buckle is from one of the four soldiers lost in Session 1. The Cult of Mars has been leaving offerings at Germanic holy sites -- not to the Vættir, but to Mars, in the Germanic style, appropriating local sacred ground to extend his territorial claim. This is investigable but not volunteered. Religion DC 15 (active: spending one minute in contact with the pole and reading its spiritual resonance): two religious traditions are active here. One old, rooted, comfortable. One new, hot, angry. They are not in harmony.
:::

**Arnulf**, a solitary Cherusci firekeeper who lives at the bog's margin, is here tending the pole when the party arrives -- or arrives shortly after, drawn by their presence. He has been leaving fresh offerings at this site for two months, ever since he found the Roman buckle, specifically to keep the Vættir from noticing the intrusion. He did not tell Thusnelda or anyone else in the village; this has been his private vigil. He will explain this plainly if asked, without shame -- *"The bog does not forgive. It only waits. I was not going to let it wake for a stranger's mistake."*

**Thusnelda's reaction if the party investigates:** *"Someone has been using our holy sites. For something else. I did not know." A long pause -- she looks at Arnulf, who says nothing. "Mars has been here. Not recently. But he has been here."*

**Cassia's herb quest completes here:** Bog valerian -- pale purple blooms, grows only in permanent bogwater -- is visible along the far bank of the water channel beside the pole. This is what she has been watching for since they crossed into the forest.

- Nature DC 13 (active: identifying the plant): A character with Nature proficiency spots it first and can point it out.
- Gathering it requires leaving the path. The channel is knee-deep and the far bank is soft ground. Perception DC 11 (passive): the soft ground is visible before stepping. Without noticing it: DC 11 Dexterity save or sink to waist-depth and need help out.
- **Mechanical payoff in Session 4:** Cassia prepares a ward compound during one overnight rest after the ritual. In Session 4, this becomes one Siege Ward -- a prepared healing station in the fort that restores 2d8 HP and removes one level of exhaustion per use (three uses before supplies are spent). Note this in your Session 4 handoff.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Encounter C: Hostile Vættir</strong> (conditional)</summary>

::: {.dm-note}
**Run this only if the party accumulated two or more disrespect triggers:** damaged a shrine, attacked the Myling, took items from the sacrifice site without acknowledgment, or ignored the boundary stone.

Vættir are not mindless undead. They are the accumulated will of the bog's dead -- protective, territorial, patient. They do not pursue outside the bog. They do not negotiate. They make the passage cost something.
:::

The path ahead narrows between two water channels. The blue-white lights in the distance multiply -- five, seven, more -- and begin moving toward the path. Not fast. Purposefully.

**Use Will-o'-Wisp stat blocks (CR 2) with these modifications:**
- They do not flee when damaged
- They cannot be turned by divine class abilities (they are spirits of place, not undead in the theological sense)
- Their damage type is cold, not lightning -- the flavor is "the cold that was in the water before it froze"
- They are dispersed (not destroyed) by Group Acknowledgment: every party member simultaneously drops one item of value into the water channels to either side of the path. One action per character, DC 10 Religion as a group to coordinate before the Vættir reach the path.

**Thusnelda if the party hesitates:** *"Into the water. Now. All of you. Into the water or we do not reach the grove."*

If the acknowledgment succeeds: the lights halt. Pause five seconds. Then they drift back into the fog one by one. The path is clear.

If the acknowledgment fails: each round, one additional Vættir joins. The party cannot outrun them through the bog. Thusnelda will perform the rite alone if the party is incapacitated -- she will succeed, but she arrives at the grove visibly exhausted and gives shorter answers for the rest of the session.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Optional Location: The Old Watching Post</strong></summary>

*(Adapted from Adventures in the Night — the mysterious interior location)*

Fifty meters off the path, visible from the high ground before the bog: four standing stones forming a small roofless chamber. Older than any Roman fortification -- pre-Celtic, possibly Neolithic. The floor is packed earth with a faint circular depression at the center: an old fire pit. Ash from within the last week.

Investigation DC 12 (active: examining the north stone): A fitted stone plug conceals a small compartment. Inside: a sealed clay flask (one dose of oil of slipperiness), a folded strip of leather with a crude hand-drawn map showing the river crossing and the grove location, and a wax tablet with a single sentence in Latin:

*IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU ARE LOOKING FOR THE SAME THING WE WERE. WE FAILED. DO NOT STOP.*

No signature. The wax is old but legible.

::: {.dm-note}
This was left by one of Vercingetorix's grandfather's warband -- the party that attempted the ritual fifty years ago, Thusnelda's failed first attempt. The map means they found the grove. The flask and tablet together tell the current party that the path is known, others have tried, and the cost was real.

If Thusnelda is present and the party shows her the tablet: *"They got further than I thought. I did not know they reached the ruins."* She does not elaborate. Her expression does.
:::

</details>

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 4: The Abandoned Village and the Ritual Site</strong></summary>

A day past the river, the forest thins into a stockade wall gone soft with rot.

::: {.dm-note}
**What this scene actually is.** This is the party's "we understand what we're actually
facing now" scene -- the moment the journey stops being about reaching the grove and
starts being about learning that the grove was never going to be enough. Everything below
still plays out in full: the village, the ritual, the skill challenge, Mars's arrival. None
of it is wasted. It just doesn't end the way anyone at the table, including Thusnelda,
expects.
:::

**Read aloud, on approach:**

> *The trees thin out ahead of a stockade wall gone soft with rot. No smoke. No dogs. A gate hangs open on one hinge, and past it, roofs have folded in on themselves under years of snow.*
>
> *Thusnelda stops walking before anyone tells her to.*
>
> *"This was my teacher's village," she says. "Before her teacher's teacher. Before the seal." She does not go on. She does not need to.*

**The village itself.** Twelve-odd longhouses, all collapsed or burned, decades of weather over both. No bodies -- whatever happened here, the dead were dealt with properly, not left to rot. This is a place that ended in ceremony, not slaughter.

**Three ways to learn what happened here (three-clue rule):**

1. **The central longhouse (obvious, no check).** Larger than the rest, its roof caved but its walls still standing. Inside: a stone table, and on it, tools -- a broken iron chisel, a shattered clay mold in the shape of a spearhead, corroded bronze pins. Someone here tried to make something to match the spear, or copy it, or unmake it. They didn't finish.

2. **The ritual circle behind the village (Investigation DC 13, active -- searching past the treeline).** Seven standing stones, twice a person's height, carved with spiraling runes that don't hold still when looked at directly. At the circle's center, the ground is fused to glass in a rough spiral, scorched black at the edges. This is the grove Thusnelda has been leading the party to. It has been used before, and it did not go well the last time.

3. **The elder's grave-marker (History DC 15, or ask Thusnelda directly -- she will answer if asked plainly, not volunteer it).** A single standing stone apart from the others, carved with a name in a script older than the runic contract tokens from the Session 1 vault. Thusnelda: *"She was the first of us. She thought the binding could be finished here, with fire and iron, blood and stone. She was certain. I have spent sixty years believing she was simply unlucky."*

**Handout opportunity:** a fragment of the shattered clay mold, or a rubbing of the elder's grave-marker script -- DM's choice which becomes a physical prop.

<details>
<summary><strong>Two Paths from the Village</strong></summary>

Past the stockade, the treeline splits around a shoulder of high ground. Thusnelda points out both without being asked:

> *"North, the old grove -- alive, still tended, once. South, the stones where my teacher's teacher tried and failed." A pause. "The stones are why we came. The grove is not required. But it is there, if any of you want to see something in this forest that isn't a wound."*

**North -- the Living Grove (optional).** A genuinely peaceful detour: green, quiet, tended in a way the ritual circle is not. Good ground for a character moment or a fight that isn't about the spear at all. See below.

**South -- the Ritual Stones (required).** The scorched circle from Clue 2. This is where the ritual happens, and where the path continues underground afterward -- see "The South Path," below.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>North Path: The Living Grove</strong> (optional)</summary>

**Read aloud:**

> *The trees here are older, and someone has kept the undergrowth clear for longer than living memory would explain. Sunlight actually reaches the ground. Birdsong, real birdsong, for the first time since the forest swallowed the road behind you. A ring of younger oaks, maybe eighty years old, grows in a rough circle around a spring-fed pool. The water is perfectly still.*

This grove belongs to no one in particular -- older than Thusnelda's order, tended out of habit and respect rather than doctrine. A **Dryad** lives here, and has for longer than anyone in the party's lifetime.

**How she reacts:** Not hostile by default. She manifests from one of the younger oaks once the party is inside the ring, and studies them before speaking -- Thusnelda she recognizes and nods to; the rest are strangers.

> *"You carry something that doesn't belong to this forest." Her eyes go to whoever is closest to the spear, or to the influenced NPC specifically if their condition shows at all. "It has been making noise for three days. I felt it before I saw you."*

**RP path.** She asks questions, not favors -- she is curious about Rome, about the spear's origin, about why the party is really here, in that order. A character who answers honestly (no check needed, just genuine roleplay) can ask one question back and get a straight answer. Good candidates for the table to ask her:
- Whether she knows anything about the elder buried to the south (she does -- *"I told her not to. She did not listen. Grief rarely does."*)
- Whether the grove can help the influenced character (she can't cure them, but she can name it aloud without flinching, which is its own small relief -- *"Whatever it is, it isn't all of you yet. Whoever wins that argument, win it before the stones."*)
- Whether Mars can reach this place (*"Not yet. This is not his war. But wars borrow ground from wherever's closest, sooner or later."*)

**Combat path, if the party is disrespectful** (drinking from or fouling the pool without asking, cutting a living tree, drawing weapons on her without provocation): she does not warn twice. She fights to drive the party out, not to kill -- Entangle, then retreat into the canopy, using **1 Dryad** plus, if the party presses the fight, **1 Brown Bear** she calls to her aid. She stops the moment the party disengages or leaves the ring; this is a grove defending itself, not a grudge.

**What the grove offers, if the party leaves it in better standing than they found it** (genuine respect, a real answer given to her honestly, or simply leaving without incident): one **Nature's Blessing** -- advantage on the next Wisdom (Survival) or Wisdom (Insight) check any one character makes before the party reaches the Skull Entrance. Small, real, not a combat boost. This is not required for anything downstream; it's a reward for engaging with content that has no plot obligation attached.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>South Path: The Ritual Stones</strong> (required)</summary>

**Optional beat, if the table needs momentum here (not required):** 2 **Vættir** or a single **Haugbui**, drawn to the old scar at the circle's center, territorial rather than hostile at first -- they attack only if the party lingers there past a clear warning. A chance to remind the table the land itself remembers what happened here, not a mandatory fight.

Survival DC 11 (active: reading the grove's physical approach before stepping inside the ring): The ground between the standing stones is clear of undergrowth in a perfect circle, but the grass has not been grazed -- it is simply absent. The stones are positioned at angles that create two natural cover positions: behind the north stone and behind the south stone. A character who notes this before the ritual begins identifies where to stand if the standing stones animate -- the cover positions displace animated stone guardian movement by one full round.

**Read aloud, at the stones:**

> *Seven standing stones ring a granite altar. Each stone is twice your height and carved with spiraling runes that don't hold still when you look at them directly — they seem to shift, rearranging themselves, as if the stone itself is thinking.*
>
> *The air is different here. Heavier. Older. The spear pulses in long, slow throbs now, like a heart slowing toward sleep.*
>
> *Thusnelda kneels at the altar. She doesn't speak immediately. Then:*
>
> *"Leave nothing at the door. What you carry in, you carry to the altar. All of it. The weapon, the doubts, and whatever part of you this journey has taken."*

<details>
<summary><strong>The Ritual Requirements</strong></summary>

Thusnelda lays out what is needed:

1. The spear must be placed on the altar, unwrapped, bare iron on stone
2. Blood from a warrior must anoint it — voluntary, 1d6 damage, cannot be healed until after the ritual
3. The group must speak in unison: *"We unmake what was made in darkness."* (in Latin or Germanic — both work)
4. A sacrifice must be offered willingly — something of genuine value, given without coercion

**The sacrifice must be real:**

| Offer | What it means | The grove's response |
|---|---|---|
| A valuable magic item | Loss of power | Acceptable |
| A proficiency | Permanently lose one skill proficiency | Acceptable |
| A memory | Choose one important memory — it's gone | Acceptable — grove returns a dream in its place |
| A year of life | Lifespan shortened | Acceptable |
| Cassia volunteers herself | Death, willingly | More than acceptable — Thusnelda tries to stop her |
| Something with no real cost | Any item worth less than the character cares about | *The altar goes cold. Nothing happens. The grove knows.* |

::: {.dm-note}
If Cassia offers herself and the party doesn't stop her: let it land as the single
heaviest option on this table, exactly as heavy as her death should be -- and it still
doesn't destroy the spear (see Conclusion, below). Nothing on this table does. That is the
point. Do not soften this by having her sacrifice be the one that "actually works" -- the
whole scene's weight depends on even the ultimate offer failing for the same reason a
smaller one would.
:::

**The influenced NPC's crisis moment:**

As the ritual begins, the influenced NPC feels the connection intensify. This is the moment they either break free or break.

If detected and supported: the party can help them resist with a group Wisdom check (DC 14). Success means they participate in the ritual and their corruption is cleared by the grove's power. Failure means they physically grab for the spear mid-ritual — not maliciously, but driven. They can be stopped without combat (Athletics grapple DC 12, or someone calling their name three times). If stopped this way, they collapse, weeping, with no memory of the last hour.

</details>

</details>

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 5: Mars Intervenes</strong></summary>

The ritual begins. The spear lights up. And Mars arrives.

Not physically. As a presence — a pressure in the air that makes the stones vibrate and causes every shadow to point toward the altar regardless of the light source. Then his voice, from everywhere and nowhere:

**Read aloud:**

> *"MORTALS."*
>
> *The word is not a sound. It moves through you like a wave, like a bell struck inside your chest.*
>
> *"YOU DARE UNMAKE WHAT A GOD FORGED."*
>
> *The standing stones crack. Not shattering — cracking, like old bones, like the grove itself is bracing for something.*
>
> *Thusnelda doesn't move. Her voice is steady:*
>
> *"Finish the ritual. Do not look up. Whatever you see, do not look up."*

<details>
<summary><strong>Three Ways to Complete the Ritual</strong></summary>

**Option A: Defensive Hold (not a winnable fight at Level 5)**

::: {.dm-note}
The standing stones are avatars of Mars' anger, not killable enemies. The party's goal is to hold them off long enough for the ritual to complete (4 successes on the Option B Skill Challenge below). Options A and B run simultaneously: some party members engage the golems while one holds the ritual. Track golem engagement: each party member actively fighting a golem keeps it occupied for 2 rounds before it pivots to the ritual holder. The golems fade automatically when the ritual completes. Do not run Option A as a combat that needs to be won.

The cover positions behind the north and south stones (spotted with Survival DC 11 before the ritual begins) displace each golem's movement by one full round when used.
:::

Mars manifests as divine wrath through the stones themselves:
- Animated Standing Stones: 3 **Stone Golems** (CR 10) but with 120 HP each — avatars of Mars' anger, not killable enemies at this level
- While some party members hold the golems back, one holds the ritual (see Option B below)
- The golems fade when the ritual completes; destroying them early buys time but is not required

**Option B: Skill Challenge — complete the ritual under pressure**

4 successes before 3 failures. Each round, one person holds the ritual while others defend:
- **Religion DC 14 (active: speaking the words of unmaking with genuine conviction)**
- **Arcana DC 15 (active: channeling the grove's ancient power, not fighting it)**
- **Athletics DC 12 (active: holding the spear steady as it fights back)**
- **Insight DC 14 (active: resisting the spear's final promise)** -- *"They'll abandon you. Take me and they won't have to."*
- **Stealth DC 13 (active: repositioning behind the standing stones before an animated golem pivots)**: Not a ritual contribution -- this is a defense move. On success, the golem wastes a movement action turning to face the new position. That round, the ritual holder has advantage on their check because the pressure source is briefly displaced.

Failures mean the ritual stumbles, and Mars' pressure increases: each failure adds one animated stone.

**Option C: Bargain -- offer Mars something before the ritual begins**

If the party steps back from the altar and speaks to Mars directly (Persuasion DC 17 or Religion DC 16, active: addressing him directly and naming what the spear has done in his name):
> *"Great Mars, the spear was being used to corrupt and destroy men in your name. We destroy it not to defy you, but because what it was doing dishonored what you stand for."*

A long silence. Then:
> *"...CONTINUE. I WILL NOT MAKE IT EASY. BUT I WILL NOT STOP IT."*

This gives advantage on all Skill Challenge rolls.

</details>

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Conclusion</strong></summary>

**Whatever happens mechanically here -- full success on the Skill Challenge, a bargain struck with Mars, or a stumbling near-failure -- the spear does not break.**

::: {.dm-note}
This is the twist the whole session has been building toward, not a fizzle. Everything
above -- the sacrifice, the golems, the skill challenge, Mars's voice -- is real and it
matters, and the mechanical outcome still has real consequences (below). It just doesn't
end the threat, because Thusnelda's entire order was wrong about where the binding
actually has to happen. Play the moment of realization as devastating for her
specifically, not as a rules technicality for the table.
:::

**Read aloud, whatever the Skill Challenge's outcome:**

> *The iron doesn't shatter. It dims — the pulsing slows, quiets, goes still, the way a fire banks down to coals instead of going out. Something in it has retreated. Nothing in it has broken.*
>
> *Thusnelda stares at the spear for a long moment. Then at the elder's grave-marker beyond the stones. Then back at the spear.*
>
> *"No," she says, very quietly, to no one. "No. We were never doing this in the right place." She looks up, and for the first time since the party met her, she looks lost. "She didn't fail because the sacrifice was wrong. She failed because this was never where it needed to happen. It happened underground. Where it was made. Where it was bound the first time."*
>
> *"I have spent my whole life tending the wrong altar."*
>
> *She turns, and points past the seventh stone. What you took for another slab of exposed rock at the circle's southern edge is a mouth -- a fissure in the hillside just wide enough to walk into, ringed with what might once have been carved teeth. Something that looks very much like a skull, if a hillside could wear one. It was here the entire time, twenty feet from where the ritual just failed.*
>
> *"There," Thusnelda says. "That is where she should have gone. That is where I should have taken you from the start."*

**If the party fully succeeded at the Skill Challenge or struck Mars's bargain:** the spear is meaningfully weakened -- its corruption pressure eases (any corruption below level 5 is reduced by 1; Level 5 characters remain affected, same as before), and Mars's presence withdraws without further violence. This was not wasted effort. It just wasn't the ending.

**If the ritual failed or was interrupted:** the spear remains at full strength, Mars's presence lingers hostile a moment longer before withdrawing, and the party carries a heavier weight into what comes next.

**Either way:** the influenced NPC's crisis moment (see above) still resolves the same way it would have -- caught or not, the corruption thread still matters going forward. The Skull Entrance is right there, at the ritual circle's own edge -- no further travel, no montage. Whatever they do next, they do it now, at the mouth of the thing they came looking for.

**Advance to Level 6**

::: {.dm-note}
**Transition to the dungeon**

The Skull Entrance sits directly off the ritual circle -- the south path from the village
ends here, not at a separate marsh requiring its own travel day. Cut straight from this
scene into Chapter 4's Scene 0 with no time skip; the marsh causeway described there is
simply the ground immediately outside this cave mouth. The party always carries the whole
spear (weakened or not, per the outcome above) into the Blood Cult Dungeon -- there is no
fragments-in-a-clay-jar branch anymore, since the spear is never destroyed here. Thusnelda
comes with them if she has earned enough trust (see her OGAS session-state table) -- this
is personal for her now, not professional courtesy. If she's present in the dungeon, she
is a witness, not a guide: she has never been past the Skull Entrance herself, and says so
plainly.

Add this to the Session 4 opening tracking table:

| Question | Session 4 implication |
|---|---|
| Did the party succeed at the grove's Skill Challenge? | Yes: the spear enters the dungeon weakened, lower corruption pressure throughout. No: full corruption pressure carries forward. Either way, the whole spear is present -- no fragment-jar variant. |
| Is Thusnelda with the party? | If yes, she is present for the dungeon's revelations as someone whose lifelong certainty just broke, not as an expert guide. |
:::

<details>
<summary><strong>Citizenship Elevation: Session 3 Window</strong></summary>

After the grove's Skill Challenge concludes and the party returns to Corvinus' reach (whether at the fort, in the field, or through a messenger he sends), Corvinus does something unexpected. He files papers.

He does not announce this. He does not explain it. A clerk appears at the party's camp or quarters with a document pouch and a brief verbal message: *"The Legate sends his regards and asks that you review the enclosed. No response is required."*

Inside the pouch, for each eligible character: a draft *commendatio* form, already completed. If the character has accumulated three or more commendationes across Sessions 1 and 2, a second document is enclosed: a formal status elevation petition, naming Corvinus as sponsor.

What it means by legal status tier:

- A *peregrinus* with three commendationes becomes eligible to petition for *Latini* standing.
- A *Latini* character with three commendationes becomes eligible for a full citizenship petition (requires a second sponsor: Tribune Lucius can serve as co-sponsor if the party treated him honorably in Session 2).
- A *cives Romani* character receives acknowledgment of distinguished service that can support a future promotion recommendation.

Corvinus does not do this out of generosity. He does it because the party has performed tasks that would be politically expensive for him to explain if they remained unthanked. He is a pragmatist. The elevation papers are institutional cover for him as much as they are reward for the party.

This window closes at Session 4 if the papers are not signed and returned. Corvinus' circumstances change, and the political calculus shifts.

::: {.dm-note}
**If the Skill Challenge failed:** Corvinus cannot file citizenship papers while the party is still in the field with a cursed spear at full strength and a siege beginning. The Session 3 citizenship window defers to the end of Session 4. The papers arrive during Session 4's conclusion scene rather than as a separate inter-session moment. The eligibility criteria are unchanged; only the timing shifts.
:::

</details>

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>DM Notes</strong></summary>

<details>
<summary><strong>OGAS This Session</strong></summary>

**Vercingetorix the Red** *(if present)*
- **Objective:** Protect his people
- **Goal (this session):** Ensure the ritual at the grove is attempted properly — this is his people's three-generation wound, and he does not yet know it won't be enough
- **Agenda:** Guide, protect, and keep the party moving toward the grove even when they want to stop
- **Secret:** He has been fighting this same war, in one form or another, since 46 BC. He does not say this -- he does not have words for it that would not sound insane -- but destroying the spear may be the first real chance he has had to die since Alesia. He will not tell anyone that either. He does not want it to change how they treat him, and some part of him does not fully believe it will happen even now.

**Thusnelda** *(new NPC)*
- **Objective:** Maintain the grove's power and fulfill her duty as its keeper — a duty she is about to discover was built on an incomplete premise
- **Goal (this session):** Get the party through the ritual correctly, exactly as she's always been taught
- **Agenda:** Be completely honest about what the ritual requires, even when that honesty is painful. She does not yet know that "correctly" isn't the same as "here."
- **Secret:** She performed this ritual once before, fifty years ago, with Vercingetorix's grandfather. It failed. She has spent sixty years certain the sacrifice was unwilling — she has never once considered that the location itself might be the problem, because that was never a possibility her teachers gave her room to imagine.

**Mars (divine presence)**
- **Objective:** Reclaim his dignity and have his weapon back
- **Goal (this session):** Stop the ritual
- **Agenda:** Apply pressure through the influenced NPC, through the grove itself, through the confrontation at the end
- **Secret:** He's been watching this party since Session 1. He respects what he's seen. He won't admit this.

**Tribune Lucius** *(if alive, with the party)*
- **Objective:** Still, underneath everything, to earn his father Brutus' respect
- **Goal (this session):** Watch the ritual to the end and decide, privately, whether Cassia and the party are right that the spear has to go
- **Agenda:** Keeps up a competent, brisk front the whole journey -- gives sound tactical advice, defers to Vercingetorix on terrain, never voices doubt aloud. He does not warn the party that his father sent him, and he does nothing to sabotage the ritual.
- **Secret:** He already suspects his father was wrong about what the spear is. Watching it destroyed (or fail to be destroyed) at the grove is the moment that suspicion becomes conviction -- see his line at the ritual's end. He has not decided what, if anything, he will do with that conviction once he returns to his father.

**Augur Cassia** *(if present)*
- **Objective:** Understand what the spear has been doing to the omens, and to her
- **Goal (this session):** Identify the sacrifice the grove will actually accept -- and privately, decide whether that sacrifice has to be her
- **Agenda:** Reads every omen honestly, even the ones that point at herself. Completes her bog valerian herb quest at the sacrifice site (Encounter B) without announcing why she needs it. Watches the influenced NPC before anyone tells her who it is -- see Clue 3.
- **Secret:** She has become increasingly certain the "genuine" sacrifice the grove wants is her own death, and she has not told anyone. Whether she acts on that belief depends entirely on how Scene 5 plays out.

**Legate Marcus Aurelius Corvinus** *(off-screen, drives Scene 3 without appearing)*
- **Objective:** Same as always: control the outcome without being the one who visibly caused it.
- **Goal (this session):** Be seen pursuing the spear without actually stopping it. He wants it destroyed as much as the party does; he cannot say so.
- **Agenda:** Sends a small, weakly-motivated escort to the river with orders soft enough to lose gracefully ("prevent the crossing," not "kill them"). Stays "one day behind" the entire session, deliberately.
- **Secret:** If the party reads the situation correctly and lets the Centurion stand down without bloodshed, Corvinus hears about it and privately considers it well handled -- this quietly helps the citizenship-elevation window at the end of the session. If the party kills his men anyway, he still can't say anything -- but it is one more loss on top of Varro's, and it shows.

**Senator Gaius Cassius Brutus (off-screen, never present this session)**
- **Objective:** Same as Session 2 -- prevent the spear from reaching Rome or being publicly resolved
- **Goal this session:** Launch Vindolanda's siege through allied chieftains while the party is in the forest; let the fort fall before the party returns
- **Agenda:** Two specific chieftains in the warband confederation owe Brutus money and old favors. They are the siege's actual organizers. Vercingetorix does not know this -- if he did, it would reframe his whole understanding of the siege. Sigrun (the Germanic trader in the vicus) knows one name if the party reaches her before leaving for the forest.
- **Secret:** Does not know about the grove ritual. His intelligence ends at the treeline. He is acting on incomplete information -- if he knew the party was attempting to destroy the spear entirely, he would not have launched the siege; he would have waited for a more controllable outcome.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>The Influenced NPC — Private Note</strong></summary>

At session start, pass the influenced player this folded note:
*"You woke last night and stood beside the spear for two hours. You don't remember doing this. The spear feels warm when you're near it. It has been making an argument, quietly, that makes a certain kind of sense: the power in this weapon could protect the people you care about. You haven't told anyone. You're not sure you're wrong."*

This player should roleplay subtle changes — nothing dramatic until the ritual. The revelation should feel earned, not shocking.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>The Sacrifice — What Works</strong></summary>

The grove is a mirror. It reflects what a character actually values versus what they claim to value. If a player tries to sacrifice something they don't care about, Thusnelda will know immediately:

> *"That is not a sacrifice. That is a fee. The grove is not a toll booth."*

The DM should know each character's central motivation (from Session 0) and gently push toward a sacrifice that actually costs something in that direction. A warrior who lives for glory might lose their greatest battle memory. A soldier who dreams of retirement might lose a year of life. A cleric who values divine connection might lose one prepared spell slot permanently.

The sacrifice is permanent. Honor it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>DM Guidance: Reading the Grove's Response</strong></summary>

The grove does not communicate clearly. It communicates correctly. Here is how to signal acceptance or rejection:

**If the sacrifice is genuine:** The altar stone warms perceptibly when the object or thing is offered. The runes on the standing stones shift slightly, as if something large turned its attention toward the altar. Thusnelda closes her eyes and exhales. She says nothing, but she opens them again looking less frightened.

**If the sacrifice is insufficient:** The altar stays cold. The offered item (or words, for intangible sacrifices) simply sits there, unreceived. Nothing dramatic happens. The absence of response is the response. Thusnelda says, quietly: *"The grove is not satisfied. Try again. You have time. Use it."*

**If the party offers nothing real at all:** After two attempts, the stones begin to cool and the grove's ambient light dims. The ritual is failing. Thusnelda: *"Something must be given or we leave here with the spear and come back when you are ready. There is no shame in it. But Mars will be closer next time."*

**The thing she will not accept:** "I sacrifice my life in the future, if necessary." The grove is not interested in conditional sacrifice. The sacrifice must be now, irrevocable, freely given. If a player offers this: Thusnelda looks at them for a moment, then: *"That is not a sacrifice. That is a bet. The grove is not a wager."*

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Commendationes This Session</strong></summary>

**Opportunity 1: seeing the ritual through to a genuine sacrifice.**
Any character actively present at the grove ritual who contributed to a successful Skill Challenge (the sacrifice was accepted, the golems held off, or Mars's bargain struck) earns one *commendatio*. Corvinus awards these through the paperwork window described above, without being told exactly what happened at the grove. He knows the party went in with a cursed weapon and came back having faced it down. That is sufficient.

**Opportunity 2: rescuing the influenced character during the ritual.**
If one character was drawn to the spear and another character physically intervened (pulled them back, broke the connection, held them when the grove's power spiked), that act of putting themselves between a colleague and a divine force qualifies. One *commendatio* to the rescuing character. This is not Corvinus' paperwork: it is Cassia's formal attestation, as the ranking officer present and the party's usual channel for this now that Varro is gone.

**Opportunity 3: protecting Vercingetorix in the forest.**
If the party defended Vercingetorix against any forest encounter (Germanic ambush, wild creature, or any threat during travel) rather than leaving him to manage his own problems, note this for Session 4. It does not become a *commendatio* yet: the reward is Vercingetorix's warriors at the gate in Session 4, and a specific moment in the epilogue.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Post-Ritual NPC States</strong></summary>

The spear is never destroyed at the grove (see Conclusion, above) — but whether the Skill Challenge succeeded still shapes how each NPC leaves this scene, and every one of them now carries the same new knowledge: the real answer is underground. Use this for Session 4 handoff.

| NPC | If the Skill Challenge succeeded | If it failed |
|---|---|---|
| **Vercingetorix** | Grimly settled, not at peace -- the wound isn't closed, but it's smaller, and he finally has somewhere real left to walk toward. | Devastated. Three generations of his family carried this wound and it is still open. He will not say it, but his face says it. |
| **Thusnelda** | Shaken but functional -- her certainty is gone, but she still knows how to move. She stays close to the party rather than turning back for the grove. | Shaken and barely functional. She sits by the elder's grave-marker for a long moment before she can speak again. Either way, she does not offer to "prepare the grove again" — she now knows there is nothing to prepare. |
| **Cassia** *(if present)* | Quiet, processing -- her visions shift in tone rather than stopping. She recognizes the underground place from a dream she's had for weeks and hadn't understood until now. | More determined than devastated. *"The omens are still bad but the shape has changed. There is still a path. I need to think."* |
| **Tribune Lucius** *(if present)* | Looks at the still-warm spear for a long time. Then: *"My father was wrong about what this was. He thought it was a political tool. He didn't know what it was."* First honest thing he's said out loud. | Practical and brisk -- this is how he handles fear. *"We need to move. The Legate is still out there. Standing here with a failed ritual and a still-active cursed weapon is a poor position."* |
| **The influenced NPC** | Whether they broke free or were pulled back during the ritual, they are quiet after. The thread is cut, or at least thinner. They feel its absence like a missing tooth -- noticeable even when nothing is wrong. Let them narrate what the absence feels like. | The thread holds. They are the most useful person in the group for what comes next, in an uncomfortable way -- they felt the spear's logic from the inside. They know how it thinks. |

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>The Influenced NPC: Roleplay Guidance for That Player</strong></summary>

At session start, when you pass the private note, also tell the player these three things to do during Scenes 1-3 -- nothing dramatic, nothing that breaks immersion, but things that will be recognisable in hindsight:

1. **Scene 1 (cold open):** When the group discovers someone was standing by the spear at night, your character is the first to suggest it might have been a sleepwalking episode or stress response. Not defensively -- genuinely, helpfully. You're trying to explain it away for yourself as much as anyone.

2. **Scene 2 (Thusnelda encounter):** When Thusnelda says *"your friend there has a thread in them"* and looks at you, your character breaks eye contact first and says something like *"She means the spear in general, doesn't she?"* -- redirecting. Again, not consciously, not maliciously. You simply cannot hold her gaze.

3. **Scene 3 (river crossing):** During the most stressful moment of the crossing, your character is unnaturally calm. Not helpful-calm -- still-calm, the way a person is still when they are listening to something no one else can hear. If anyone asks, you have no explanation for it.

These three moments should not be pointed out by the DM. They are for the player to plant and the other players to notice, or not, until the ritual makes it undeniable.

This session should feel like the pressure never fully releases. The investigation of the cold open mystery, the river crossing, the abandoned village, the grove itself — there's no safe moment, and the grove doesn't end it either. Push toward the grove, then push past the realization that the grove was never enough. The forest is hostile to lingering.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Skill Audit: Session 3</strong></summary>

**Forest travel: spread skill demands across the table.**

The travel events should each call on a different character's strength. Check this before you run. Nobody should dominate the forest crossing. The table below shows the primary approach, a backup approach (different door, not failed door), and where applicable a third approach using skills that might otherwise have nothing to do in this session.

| Event | Primary skill | Alternative | Third option |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wind-felled oak | Athletics DC 12 (active: clearing or climbing the obstacle) | Survival DC 10 (active: finding a safe path around) | Stealth DC 12 (active: if the party wants to pass without announcing themselves to whoever felled it -- a fallen oak on a travel path is sometimes deliberate) |
| Hanging charms | Persuasion DC 13 (active: passing without giving offense) | Religion DC 11 (passive: understand the boundary and perform a basic acknowledgment rite -- no social check, just knowledge) | -- |
| Silent animal trail | Survival DC 12 (active: tracking by sign) | Nature DC 14 (active: identifying the specific predator -- wolf signs vs. something else changes the response entirely) | -- |
| Old Roman standard | Investigation DC 12 (active: reading dates and unit markings) | History DC 14 (passive: naming the expedition and what happened to it; this lands harder when they know the story) | -- |
| Boggy hollow | Acrobatics DC 12 (active: crossing without sinking) | Nature DC 10 (active: reading the plants and identifying firm ground; avoids the roll entirely) | Medicine DC 11 (passive: recognizing bog fever risk from the water type; warns against resting here, which costs time but prevents the exhaustion check) |
| Watchful raven | Insight DC 12 (active: reading it correctly -- omen, not threat) | Animal Handling DC 10 (active: acknowledging it respectfully; the raven leaves satisfied) | -- |
| Blood-slick stones | Religion DC 14 (passive: reading the runes) | Investigation DC 12 (active: dating the sacrifice; within 24 hours changes everything) | Sleight of Hand DC 12 (active: pocketing a rune-carved offering stone without the group noticing -- optional, morally complicated) |
| Whispering pines | Wisdom save DC 12 | Performance DC 12 (active: giving the whispers a response that satisfies them; costs one round but removes the disadvantage) | Deception DC 13 (active: convincing yourself the whispers are wind, not a real voice; a successful self-deception suppresses the Wisdom save but prevents any meaningful information from the pines) |
| Germanic patrol (if added) | Persuasion DC 14 (active: speaking any Germanic phrase from the player guide) | Intimidation DC 13 (active: a show of force before weapons are drawn; they don't want this fight either) | Deception DC 15 (active: claiming to be friendly traders; requires something tangible to sell the claim) |

*Note: the Germanic patrol is not on the d8 table above but can be substituted for any roll of 3 if Vercingetorix is not with the party.*

**Medicine DC 13 (active: examining the influenced NPC when Clue 1 appears):**

A character with Medicine proficiency who examines them physically -- checks their pulse, looks at their eyes, feels their skin temperature -- finds elevated heart rate, dilated pupils inconsistent with the light level, and a slight fever. These are not illness markers. They are arousal markers: the body in pre-combat readiness, with the mind still calm. The character examining them knows that combination from battlefield experience. Something is priming them. The body knows before the mind does.

**Stealth DC 13 (active: approaching a Germanic patrol or shrine without being detected):**

Before any social encounter in the forest, the party can choose to observe first. Stealth as a group check (weakest roller determines success) lets them see the patrol or shrine before being seen. Success gives them one round of assessment before engagement. On a critical success (5 above DC), they observe long enough to determine intent -- whether the patrol is searching, resting, or actively tracking.

**Deception DC 14 (active: passing as non-Roman travelers during an unexpected Germanic encounter):**

Requires either non-Roman equipment (no lorica segmentata visible, Germanic cloaks) or a convincing story. A character with a Germanic background or Vercingetorix vouching reduces this to DC 10. A character in full legionary kit attempting this without cover has DC 18 and disadvantage.

**Intimidation DC 14 (active: at the river crossing, ordering the pursuing legionaries to stand down):**

As described in the crossing scene. On 5 above the DC: the opposing centurion signals his men to hold and does not cross.

**Temporal gate: river crossing boot print:**

One round. Only if someone is watching the bank rather than the river.

- *Perception DC 11 (active: watching the near bank specifically while others watch the water):* Military sandal, size 10, made within the last two hours, heading north. Corvinus has scouts ahead of them.
- *What it opens:* They can send a decoy, move off the main path, or prepare for scouts at the grove. Without this read, Corvinus's scouts are already watching when they arrive. One check, one round. Make it count.
- *Why the window closes:* Rain washes it. The crossing scene ends, the rain intensifies, the print is gone. That is what rain does to boot prints in mud.

**Thusnelda trust: the first meeting.**

Do not move this entirely through narrative. The key moment is when she decides whether to lead them to the grove. Give it a DC.

- *Persuasion DC 14 (active: backed by something genuine -- sparing a prisoner, a gift, Vercingetorix vouching):* She leads them.
- *Persuasion DC 18 (active), or Germanic language proficiency, or Religion DC 15 (active: speaking her ritual language):* She leads them AND volunteers the piece of grove knowledge they did not know to ask for: the lock in the altar's northwest face, and what it opens.
- *Fail:* She says "Tomorrow." That is not a refusal. The party camps in the forest for one night. One additional forest event occurs overnight. The window does not close: it costs time. That is the right consequence.

**Ritual skill challenge (Option B):**

Annotated for ease of reference:

- *Religion DC 14 (active: speaking the words of unmaking with genuine conviction):* Fail by 4 or less -- the words come out but without power. The grove receives them as intent, not invocation. Not a wasted round, but not a success. Try differently next time.
- *Arcana DC 15 (active: channeling the grove's ancient power rather than overriding it):* The hardest check because it requires surrendering the reflex to control the magic. A character who has taken arcane damage (from the spear) this session has advantage.
- *Athletics DC 12 (active: holding the spear steady as it fights back):* The spear weighs what it weighs until the ritual begins. After, it pulls. This check is simply whether a character is strong enough to keep it on the altar.
- *Insight DC 14 (active: resisting the spear's final promise):* The promise is specific to the character holding the spear. The DM should know what it will offer each character from Session 0 material. The promise is not generic fear -- it is the thing the character most wants, offered at the worst possible moment.

<details>
<summary><strong>Cascade unlock: Vercingetorix's dying admission</strong> (DM only)</summary>

This only becomes available after the ritual, when the party has shown what they are made of. A genuine sacrifice opens it; a token sacrifice does not. That is not a punishment: it is Vercingetorix applying the same standard he applies to everyone.

- DC 14 Insight after the ritual to notice he is holding something back.
- If a player asks directly: he tells them.
- The admission: he knew three months ago that Brutus's agents were in contact with two of the warband chieftains surrounding Vindolanda. He did not say anything because he was not sure the party was worth trusting with information that would get them killed. Now he is sure.
- What it opens in Session 4: the party can split the siege by targeting those specific chieftains. Sigrun knows more if they can reach her. Write this in your Session 4 notes now.

</details>

</details>

</details>
